title: PolyFEMBlenderPlugin: physics simulation without leaving Blender

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: You model a scene in Blender, but to simulate how it deforms you'd normally juggle files and command lines. This add-on keeps it all in one place.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: So it connects Blender to a physics solver?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Yes. It's an experimental Blender extension that turns selected objects, materials and contact settings into a setup file for PolyFEM, a finite-element solver, then runs the simulation. Antoine wrote it for simulation work at the ÉTS lab.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: What do I do inside Blender?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: A PolyFEM panel in the Physics tab lets you pick a material preset like steel or aluminium, set contact, time and boundary conditions, then create the setup file. Meshes are exported, and TetWild can turn them into tetrahedral meshes.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: It runs PolyFEM in the background, using a Docker image or a local program. When it finishes, a Render Animation button imports each step as a mesh and keyframes them, so you play the result back as an animation.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: A neat loop from scene to simulation to playback. It needs Blender four point two or later, and the write-up has the full workflow.
